summary: Phase C (Standalone Crew Bank) full-stack verification. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_phase_c.py (36 tests, xdist-safe RUN_PREFIX 'TEST_userC_', full teardown) covering POST/GET/GET-mine/PATCH-status/POST-renew/DELETE on /api/crew-bank/standalone plus Phase A/B regression — 36/36 passed. Re-ran test_phase_a.py + test_phase_b.py untouched: 53/53 passed. Frontend /crew-bank tested via Playwright with mongo-minted premium and free sessions: anon empty state, paid listing flow (create -> mine-summary -> found/reopen -> renew -> remove), free-tier upsell gate, DM link on other sailors' cards, and market scoping all work. No blocking issues found.

minor.issue: `count` is the page size (len(entries)) after the limit/skip, not the total matching listings. Once >60 sailors are listed the UI cannot show a true total or paginate.
Query allows expires_at:None as 'never expires'. No endpoint ever writes null, so this branch is dead but would silently expose any manually inserted permanent listing.
No length caps on experience/notes/availability strings (StandaloneCrewUpsert has no max_length), and positions/markets lists are unbounded — a client can store arbitrarily large text/arrays.
Stores user_bio in the doc but no endpoint/UI consumes it; dead field (cosmetic).

issues: Sonner toasts render top-center and overlay the header nav, covering the 'Events'/'Crew Bank' links for the toast duration — nav items are unclickable while a toast is up. Consider top-right or below-header offset.

Own listing correctly disappears from the public grid, but the grid then shows the generic 'No sailors listed yet.' empty state while the 'Your listing' block still says Found a boat — slightly confusing; an inline 'your listing is hidden while marked found' hint would help.

action_items: Optional: return a true total count (count_documents) alongside the page in GET /api/crew-bank/standalone and add skip/pagination for >60 listings.
Optional: add max_length constraints to StandaloneCrewUpsert (experience/notes/availability) and cap positions/markets list sizes.
Optional UX: offset toasts so they don't overlay header nav links on /crew-bank.
critical_code_review_comments: All six standalone endpoints correctly exclude _id, and the public list projects out user_email; /mine correctly returns it to the owner only — verified by assertions.
Upsert uses $setOnInsert for created_at so re-POST preserves creation time, refreshes expires_at (+90d) and never duplicates (countDocuments == 1) — verified.

Paid gating uses server-side is_paid_subscriber (402 for free) and the frontend gate is only cosmetic — correct defense-in-depth; free-tier POST is rejected server-side even if the disabled button is bypassed.
CrewBank.jsx is ~306 lines and readable, but the standalone modal form body is a good candidate for extraction if more fields are added.
seed_data_creation: Mongo-minted TEST_userC_* users/sessions (premium/featured/basic/free) and crew_bank_standalone docs; all deleted after the run (crew_bank_standalone count back to 0, no TEST_userC_* users remain). seed crew.alex identity_verified=true preserved and asserted.
test_credentials: No app passwords. Mint mongo sessions per /app/auth_testing.md; helper mint_user() in tests/test_phase_c.py (set subscription_tier for paid gating).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase C backend + frontend fully green. Suites: test_phase_a.py (Phase A), test_phase_b.py (Boat Pro creds/tier + enriched authors), test_phase_c.py (standalone crew bank). All use subprocess mongosh against test_database with RUN_PREFIX teardown; run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_phase_c.py -p no:randomly -q`. Frontend auth = session_token cookie on domain nw-sailing-community.preview.emergentagent.com. NOTE for UI tests: openForm() pre-selects the user's primary_market, so clicking sa-market-<primary_market> DESELECTS it — pick a different market instead. External requests need a browser User-Agent.
rca_of_the_issue: No defects reproduced. One initial test failure ('Pick at least one market') was a test-script error: the standalone modal pre-selects the user's primary market and my click toggled it off. Corrected the script; app behavior is correct.
